newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boost from U.S. keeps German shares on record run.
newsitem.headline: Boost from U.S. keeps German shares on record run.

text.p: German shares were inspired by the U.S. to continue their record-breaking run early on Wednesday, as an upbeat report from the Fed's Greenspan, a strong close on Wall St and a firm dollar lifted the IBIS DAX.
The IBIS DAX was up 107.59 points, or 2.50 percent, at 4,405.23 at 0747 GMT, having earlier breached the 4,400-point barrier for the first time.
"The banks are up, the cars are up. The DTB options guys are starting to buy. Everything is good as gold as far as I can see," a Frankfurt trader said.
The dollar trading around 1.82 marks underpinned sentiment.

Other helpful news from the U.S. came in the shape of a speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who said the central bank might rise interest rates to head off inflation, but suggested this might not happen anytime soon.

Greenspan's comments drove the Dow Jones Industrial index higher as investors interpreted Greenspan's comments as suggesting that Fed policy was on hold and the Dow ended the day up nearly two percent.
Traders said that this gave a valuable boost to the German share market, which has taken its lead from the Dow for many of its moves during the recent bull run.
"The whole Greenspan thing was phenomenally bullish as far as I'm concerned," the broker said.
Bulls prevailed in terms of measuring the outlook for the DAX. One trader said he saw a technical buy signal and said that he saw the DAX hitting 4,500 points in the near term.
Shares in the limelight early on included Deutsche Bank AG, which rose over nine percent in pre-bourse trade after it reported better-than-expected results for the first half of 1997.
The group reported a 27.5 percent rise in group net income to 1.5 billion marks in the first half of 1997.
"I think it was bank merger speculation and short-covering which was helping Deutsche early on, more than the figures," a trader said.

Seven out of the ten top gainers in IBIS trade were banks, including Bayerische Vereinsbank up 13.25 marks -- 13.25 percent -- at 113.25 marks and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, up 5.60 marks, 7.52 percent, at 80.10 marks.
Both of these banks have been the focus of market attention for the last few days since they announced their intention to merge into one Bavarian super-bank.
Chemical stocks also had a good run, especially BASF AG, up 90 pfennigs at 71 marks, and Bayer AG, up one mark at 76.50 marks.
